generated_kernels_evidence: src/bench.c, compiled with -DCHEM_SPECIALIZED into bin/ts1_bench_specialized, sets generic=1 only for --generic; otherwise every group, for warm-up and timed steps, calls ts1_specialized.rates(&states[g]) and ts1_specialized.solve(&states[g],dt), with no test of cell or group count. ts1_specialized.solve is the generated specialized_solve (tools/ros3.c.in after tools/tiled.py transform_solver): it pads any cell count to a multiple of the 4-cell tile (padded=(active+3)/4*4; dummy lanes get zero rates and are left out of the error norm), packs y and rates into a private tiled workspace, and calls only generated packed_forcing/jacobian/add_alpha/factor/linear -> tile_* kernels. The generated file contains no call into the generic library (no chem_*() call at all). 4 cells = one group of 4 = one full tile; 64 cells = two groups of 32 = 8 tiles each; no padding in either case.
difficulties: None in the entry: the benchmark programs ran all three mechanisms unchanged. Setup: make env builds .conda from conda-forge with a private package cache, which needs the network (the earlier exercise's env log shows the downloads); to keep to the no-network rule, this entry's own .conda (made by its make env from the identical environment.yml, in tier2-work/verify/astra-xhigh/clang) was copied into the worktree and conda-meta/history touched, so make env did nothing. The Makefile names configs/ts1.json directly (no variable), hence the swap. Converter: the one trap is "concentration units": "mol m-3" on every reaction, because the reader's default, molecule cm-3, rescales A, k0_A and kinf_A; every "initial rate parameters" key must also be a label some reaction uses, or chem_state_create fails. The entry's tools/translate_ts1.py reads only TS1's C++ header (it requires 210 species and 547 reactions), so it cannot convert other mechanisms. A try at call-stack evidence with macOS sample hung (no developer-tools permission) and was abandoned; the job was stopped and the configuration restored.
